title: NEXT-046
universal_lens: Webhook retry/dead-letter layer forms a commutative diagram: exponential-backoff stochastic process (retry kernel) → absorbing Markov state (dead-letter) → information-theoretic observability functional, all constrained by safety-gate predicates ensuring zero production leakage.
gsi_mapping: GSI treats each webhook attempt as a Bayesian trial: prior = delivery success probability; likelihood = observed latency/error codes; posterior updates retry policy hyperparameters. Conformal prediction yields finite-sample coverage guarantees on dead-letter absorption time.
gse_mapping: GSE models webhook lifecycle as state-transition system: {PENDING, RETRYING(n), DELIVERED, DEAD_LETTER}. Transition kernel incorporates exponential backoff with jitter. Safety gates enforce invariant: ∀t, production_data_access(t) = ∅ until owner_approval = 1.

primitives.name: Exponential Backoff Retry Kernel
primitives.verbatim_quote: # NEXT-046: Webhook retry and dead-letter layer ## Repo(s) Trigger.dev ## Category Autonomous Workers ## Goal Implement or design the webhook retry and dead-letter layer capability for GSE / GSN without touching production data first.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: T_k: retry timestamp [s]; B: base delay [s]; J: jitter bound [s]; T_max: max delay cap [s]; k: attempt index [dimensionless]
primitives.assumptions: Independent failure events; stationary error distribution; bounded network latency; jitter uniform on [0,J]
primitives.breakdown_regime: B·2^k > T_max triggers saturation; correlated failures violate independence; unbounded latency breaks convergence

layer2.mapping: GSE state-transition: RETRYING(k) → RETRYING(k+1) with probability p_fail; → DELIVERED with probability 1-p_fail. GSI: p_fail ~ Beta(α,β) updated per attempt.
layer2.telemetry: Empirical CDF of inter-attempt intervals; Kaplan-Meier estimator for delivery survival function

primitives.name: Dead-Letter Absorption Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: # NEXT-046: Webhook retry and dead-letter layer ## Repo(s) Trigger.dev ## Category Autonomous Workers ## Goal Implement or design the webhook retry and dead-letter layer capability for GSE / GSN without touching production data first.
primitives.latex: P = \begin{pmatrix} Q & R \\ 0 & I \end{pmatrix}, \quad Q_{ij} = \mathbb{P}(X_{t+1}=j | X_t=i, i,j \in \mathcal{T}), \quad R_{i\ell} = \mathbb{P}(X_{t+1}=\ell | X_t=i, i \in \mathcal{T}, \ell \in \mathcal{A})
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: P: transition matrix [dimensionless]; Q: transient-to-transient [dimensionless]; R: transient-to-absorbing [dimensionless]; 𝒯: transient states {PENDING, RETRYING(1..K)}; 𝒜: absorbing states {DELIVERED, DEAD_LETTER}
primitives.assumptions: Finite state space; time-homogeneous transitions; absorption certain (I-Q invertible); max retries K < ∞
primitives.breakdown_regime: Infinite retry loop (K→∞) makes Q non-substochastic; non-Markovian dependencies (e.g., rate limiting memory) violate homogeneity

layer2.mapping: GSE: absorption time τ ~ PhaseType(α, Q) where α = initial distribution. GSI: conformal prediction interval for τ at level 1-δ using calibration set of historical webhook traces.
layer2.telemetry: Absorption probability vector B = (I-Q)^{-1}R; mean time to absorption μ = (I-Q)^{-1}1; dead-letter rate = B_{DEAD_LETTER}

primitives.name: Safety Gate Predicate
primitives.verbatim_quote: Do not emit live notifications, billing events, or public AI output without owner approval.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: Γ: safety predicate [Boolean]; σ: system state [dimensionless]; access_p: data access function for production resource p [Boolean]; approval_p: owner approval flag [Boolean]
primitives.assumptions: Approval flags immutable during execution; access_p decidable at compile-time; no side-channel leakage
primitives.breakdown_regime: Race condition between approval check and access; dynamic code loading bypasses static analysis; approval revocation not propagated

layer2.mapping: GSE: deployment guard — transition to LIVE state only if Γ(σ)=1. GSI: Bayesian network with Γ as deterministic node; posterior P(leak|Γ=1)=0 by construction.
layer2.telemetry: Static analysis pass rate; runtime guard evaluation latency [μs]; false-negative rate on penetration tests

primitives.name: Observability Entropy Functional
primitives.verbatim_quote: ## Founder/Internal Value The team gets measurable workflows, fewer manual steps, better observability, and clearer build priorities.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: H: Shannon entropy [bits]; 𝒪: observability event space; ℙ(o): empirical frequency of observable o [dimensionless]
primitives.assumptions: Ergodic sampling of webhook traces; observables sufficient for policy optimization; stationarity over calibration window
primitives.breakdown_regime: Non-stationary error distributions (e.g., upstream API changes); insufficient observables (hidden confounders); sampling bias from disabled-by-default flag

layer2.mapping: GSI: H[𝒪] quantifies information gain per webhook trace; used in Bayesian experimental design for retry policy A/B tests. GSE: entropy gradient ∇_θ H drives build priority ranking via mutual information I(θ; 𝒪).
layer2.telemetry: Rolling entropy estimate over sliding window; mutual information between retry policy params and delivery outcome; alert on entropy drop > 2σ

reasoning_traces.think:
The webhook retry/dead-letter layer decomposes into four mathematically coupled primitives. The retry kernel (T_{k+1} = T_k + min(B·2^k + U(0,J), T_max)) defines a non-homogeneous Poisson process with state-dependent rate λ_k = 1/E[T_{k+1}-T_k]. This maps to GSE's RETRYING(k) state transitions where p_fail(k) = 1 - exp(-λ_k Δt). The dead-letter absorption operator constructs a finite absorbing Markov chain with transient states 𝒯 = {PENDING, RETRYING(1..K)} and absorbing states 𝒜 = {DELIVERED, DEAD_LETTER}. The fundamental matrix N = (I-Q)^{-1} yields exact absorption probabilities B = NR and mean absorption times μ = N1. GSI exploits this: conformal prediction on historical τ ~ PhaseType(α,Q) gives distribution-free coverage intervals for dead-letter SLA. The safety gate predicate Γ(σ) = ⋀_p (access_p(σ)=∅ ∨ approval_p=1) is a compile-time decidable Boolean lattice that enforces zero production leakage — a hard constraint in GSE's deployment automaton. Observability entropy H[𝒪] = -Σ ℙ(o) log ℙ(o) over {attempt_count, latency, error_code, dead_letter_reason} provides the information-theoretic signal for both GSI's Bayesian policy updates (mutual information I(θ;𝒪) guides hyperparameter search) and GSE's build prioritization (entropy gradient ∇_θ H ranks feature impact). Failure modes couple: retry saturation (B·2^k > T_max) increases dead-letter absorption probability non-linearly; safety gate bypass correlates with observability blind spots (low H[𝒪] masks leakage). The commutative diagram requires: retry kernel → absorption operator → entropy functional, all constrained by Γ=1.

reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: Exponential backoff originates from Ethernet CSMA/CD (1976) and TCP retransmission (Jacobson 1988). Absorbing Markov chains formalized by Kemeny & Snell (1960). Phase-type distributions for absorption times (Neuts 1981). Conformal prediction (Vovk et al. 2005) provides finite-sample guarantees. Safety gates derive from capability-based security (Dennis & Van Horn 1966) and zero-trust architectures. reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: Upstream API providers act as adversarial environment: rate limits induce correlated failures violating retry kernel independence. Malicious webhook payloads target safety gate bypass via confused deputy attacks. Internal teams face misaligned incentives: product wants faster retries (lower B), reliability wants higher T_max, security wants Γ=1 always. Owner approval process introduces human latency — model as stochastic delay with heavy-tailed distribution.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: Anti-collinearity: retry kernel parameters (B,J) must be identifiable from observability entropy H[𝒪] — veto if Fisher information matrix det(I(θ)) < ε. Leakage veto: any code path with access_p(σ)≠∅ must have static proof of Γ(σ)=1 — veto on dynamic imports or eval(). Conformal coverage veto: if empirical dead-letter rate exceeds 1-δ+η for calibrated δ, freeze deployment. Entropy stationarity veto: reject policy updates if H[𝒪] drift > 2σ over 24h window.
